quote: He took our 2 year old son off my hands for about 30 minutes last night because I am in my first trimester with our second and exhausted and needed a rest
cx: A working mother, first trimester of her second, with a stay-at-home-dad husband.

quote: I work full time (and then some, demanding job) he works part time while he looks for a more stable job, I do more childcare, he does more housework. I think we are both pulling our weight as best we can.
cx: How the couple split the load in her second pregnancy.

quote: Now that I am pregnant, he’s terrified and thinks his life is ending. I am getting frustrated and annoyed by his constant comments about how he won’t be able to do anything once the baby gets here.
cx: 30 weeks, first baby; her husband spends each weekend out hiking.

quote: He wants to go hiking ALL DAY and I am not physically able to do the trails he wants to. […] Hiking in 90 degree weather is just not doable for me.
cx: Why she stays home alone on his days off.

quote: I wish fathers had to go the nine months before the baby arrives feeling and experiencing and worrying about the stuff mothers do. It drives me mad.
cx: Same post.

quote: He helped build the dresser but that’s really it. I have done everything else. I have everything ready (and it’s beautiful 💕) but he is less ready and more stressed than me somehow! I’m the one giving birth soon😭 I signed us up for birthing and newborn classes since he is so stressed about the baby.
cx: Who has done the preparing, at 30 weeks.

quote: I am a SPED teacher and giving birth right at the start of the school year. I wanted to take some time off because I can’t imagine leaving my baby to be with other kids all day and when daycare costs so much.
cx: Her plan for work after the birth.

quote: she brought me to see a baby changing table/dresser that she had gotten for a steal. […] She looked really confused for a second before replying with "Oh no, this is for my house, when she stays here with us."
cx: 25 weeks with her first; the mother-in-law is furnishing her own home for overnight stays.

quote: Both my mother and MIL have been getting too excited and showing me gifts that they got second handed, mostly clothes, breast feeding/pregnancy pillows, and diapers.
cx: What the grandmothers have gathered for the baby.

quote:
\-mil and fil bought a crib and walker for their house before before my fiancé and i even had one  
\-i’m due in early december and had brought up not taking baby out for holidays to which mil kind of dismissed my concerns  
\-frequently talks about how she’s excited to be in the delivery room but i also haven’t shut the idea down
cx: 20 weeks; early signs with a future mother-in-law next door.

quote: fiancé says “if we can’t trust you to follow a simple rule with the dog, then we won’t be able to trust you to respect our wishes with the baby” mil then begins crying and accuses fiancé of holding the baby against her. […] she continues on to say “you’re gonna upset me and you’re gonna regret it”
cx: A small rule broken at a family party becomes a test case for the baby.

quote: We basically have about 5 weeks to flip our lives around and get things ready for a child we didnt expect.
cx: A husband whose wife learned at about 35 weeks that she was pregnant.

quote: My sister in law basically jumped in to help get a registry set up and reach out to people for donations and all that
cx: Who helped them get ready in five weeks.

quote: she also informed me (not asked) that they are coming to visit 2 weeks after my due date (not staying with us though) and that my baby better be born by then so she can see them. Which just gave me the ick.
cx: Weeks from her second birth; the mother-in-law lives across the country.

quote: She has a lot of wants and expectations from us, like coming to visit them with our two small children when they dont have any baby gear and we would have to bring absolutely everything we need (stroller, crib, changing mat, car seats, toys clothes and so forth)
cx: What visiting the distant grandmother would mean with two under three.

quote: i just feel like she is demanding a lot and contributing very little to the "village".
cx: Same post.

quote: It progressed quickly- I was yelling in my tub, trying to entertain my toddler with a water tea party while my fiancee tried to get our belongings together, make bfast (because I asked), and watch a 2 year old.
cx: Six months on, her second labour at home while her mother sat downstairs.

quote: when she said sorry she told me I didn’t communicate well enough that I was in labor (I texted and was obviously screaming) and that I didn’t want her help before so she didn’t feel like I wanted her to come upstairs.
cx: Her mother's explanation afterwards.

quote: She makes comments like “you’re never gonna see that baby!! You’ll never be able to take it off me!” Or “your mum and my mum will be fighting over baby! We’ll have to make appointments!” Or my personal favourite “as soon as you have baby I’m taking it and I’m locking myself in my bedroom so no one can come in!!”
cx: Due in December, first grandchild on both sides.

quote: She’s also said “nobody is going to want to see you anymore they are just going to want baby,”
cx: Another of her mother-in-law's lines.

quote: My partner says all the right things though thank goodness, like “that’s why WE are the parents and WE set boundaries and make the choices,” but he also comes to her defense like “you know she wouldn’t actually do that she’s just excited,”
cx: What her partner says when she raises his mother's comments.

quote: His girlfriend immediately got a little irritated and said, “You’re our only option.” […] Then my brother suggested we “play it by ear” and see if I’ve had the baby by then.
cx: 38 weeks, first baby; asked to babysit a 5-year-old four days before her due date.

quote: Instead of checking in to see if I need anything or asking how they can support me, they’ve just tried to give me tasks like watching their pets and babysit. They’re also trying to get my mom to babysit for them when she comes out to help me with the baby when my husband returns to work, so they can go rafting.
cx: Her mother is flying in to cover the weeks after her husband's leave ends.
